posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
I'm over here at Notre Dame in South Bend, and saw an interesting abstract in SciFinder: "Dichromated gelatin holograms with triphenyl dyes" in SPIE 6912 (2008) Practical Holography XXII: Materials and Applications.

Has anyone seen this paper yet?

posts.author: Martin
posts.content_md:
> **Joe Farina:** I'm over here at Notre Dame in South Bend, and saw an interesting abstract in SciFinder: "Dichromated gelatin holograms with triphenyl dyes" in SPIE 6912 (2008) Practical Holography XXII: Materials and Applications.Has anyone seen this paper yet?

Not that particular one but another, probably similar one: Sharlandjiev/Markova, On fabrication of large format optoelectronic elements. It's here: [http://joam.infim.ro/JOAM/pdf5_1/Sharlandjiev.pdf](http://joam.infim.ro/JOAM/pdf5_1/Sharlandjiev.pdf)

That Bulgarian group used triphenylmethane and thiasine dyes for red-sensitized DCG. Their system only consists of dichromate and one of these dyes – so this is nothing like Jeff's TMG system.

I assume speed is inferior to Jeff's system but has the advantage of being fully compatible with “normal” DCG.

posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
If you havent seen it, take a look at [http://spie.org/x648.xml?product_id=760989](http://spie.org/x648.xml?product_id=760989) 

The exact dyes weren't listed on the SciFinder abstract either. The authors made a couple of claims in the abstract, like "excellent resolution and behavior" and "...dyes...that increase the photo sensibility respect to conventional DCG and is easy to use" and I was wondering what they were talking about.

posts.content_md:

The authors made a couple of claims in the abstract, like "excellent resolution and behavior" and "...dyes...that increase the photo sensibility respect to conventional DCG and is easy to use" and I was wondering what they were talking about.

OK, thanks. My guess would be these are similar dyes (at least the same dye family) as the ones mentioned in the pdf file I pointed to. Unlike Jeff's TMG system I believe these dyes don't require a particular pH regime. I assume this is simply “normal” DCG + a “triphenyl dye”.

I assume the “speed increase” the authors mention, refers to a wavelength range outside the 350 – 450nm, where “normal” DCG is fastest...

Thinking on photosensitive coatings there is an option of use diazonium salts:(Extract from a Kuraray document)

*The commercially available special diazonium compounds are stable for long periods at room temperature. Onlywhen exposed to short-wave light (maximum absorption between 300 and 450 nm) does photolytic cleavage of the NNarrangement take place in the molecule, followed by the substitution of hydroxyl groups. As a result, thedecomposition products manufactured in this way are able to form water-insoluble complexes with PVOH.*

Any info available about gelatine use??
